title: Every omega-tree with finite levels contains a leafless balanced subtree with omega levels

standard_prerequisites.name: The notion of a balanced subtree and of the degree of a node on a level
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Defined in the paragraphs preceding the counted statement (the discussion ending at source line 489)
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes what has to be produced and what the pruning at each stage must achieve.

standard_prerequisites.name: A sequence of natural numbers in which every number occurs infinitely often
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at lines 494-495 and 508
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the schedule according to which the successive prunings are performed and why each level is handled infinitely often.

core_obligations: Fix a schedule: choose a sequence of natural numbers in which every number occurs infinitely often, and build a decreasing sequence of subtrees T_n of T, each still having omega levels (proof lines 494-499).

Perform one pruning step: given T_n, let X_n consist of the nodes of height k_n with infinitely many points above them and, subject to that, minimum degree, and obtain T_{n+1} by deleting everything above the members of the k_n-th level outside X_n; the result still has omega levels (proof lines 500-506).

Show the intersection is what is wanted: for a fixed n the levels of the T_m at height n form a decreasing sequence of non-empty finite sets, hence are eventually constant and equal the n-th level of the intersection T* (proof lines 508-511).

Conclude balance and leaflessness: every node of the n-th level of T* has a successor in every T_m and hence in T*, so it is not a leaf, and its degree is the same for all nodes of that level; hence T* is a balanced subtree with omega levels and no leaves (proof lines 511-513).
proof_roadmap: Schedule the prunings along a sequence hitting every level infinitely often, and prune so that the surviving nodes of the scheduled level have minimum possible degree (proof lines 494-506).
Take the intersection and use eventual constancy of the levels plus the existence of successors to get balance and absence of leaves (proof lines 508-513).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, inside any tree with omega finite levels, a subtree that is balanced, has no leaves and still has omega levels (statement lines 491-492). The proof schedules prunings according to a sequence in which every natural number occurs infinitely often, at each stage keeping only the nodes of the scheduled level that have infinitely many points above them and, among those, the minimum degree, and then takes the intersection of the resulting decreasing sequence of subtrees (proof lines 494-506). The two steps that carry the content are the choice of the minimum-degree pruning, which is what produces equal degrees on each level, and the argument that the levels of the intersection are eventually constant, which uses that each level is scheduled infinitely often and the levels are finite (proof lines 500-511). Leaflessness then follows because nodes survive with successors at every stage. H2.
